question: A dealer allows his customers a discount of 18% and still gains 24%. If an article costs ₹1,560 to the dealer, what is its marked price (to the nearest ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the ratio formula: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

1560 / MP = (100 − 18) / (100 + 24) = 82 / 124

MP = 1560 × (124 ÷ 82) = 1560 × 1.51219...

MP ≈ ₹2359.02

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2359.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹1,560

Profit% = 24%

Discount% = 18%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100
